subject: Inference qualification & benchmark proposal — next tests and access
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@novushealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + proposed benchmark plan

Tom — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete next steps I promised: 

- What we heard: Novus wants an apples-to-apples latency + throughput comparison between (A) Novus using their current hyperscaler API and (B) Redwood Hosted / Dedicated serving the same model family. Key success metrics: p95 and p99 latency for 512-token responses, sustained tokens/sec for 1k concurrent sessions, and end-to-end tail latency under client network conditions.
- Constraints you mentioned: can't share production data, but can run a synthetic prompt set (we suggested subset attached) and provide ephemeral eval accounts. Procurement wants cost estimates and an SOC2 addendum before tests start.

Proposed lab plan (high level):
1) We'll run 2 A/B sweeps over the same prompts: one against their hyperscaler endpoint, one against a Redwood Dedicated instance configured to match GPU class. Each sweep: 5k requests, 512 max tokens, warm KV-cache runs (3 warm passes) then steady-state.
2) Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side), tokens/sec (aggregate), tokens/sec per GPU, retry/error rates, and per-request tail size.
3) Config matrix: batch sizes [1,4,8], kv-cache enabled/disabled, quantized model (int8) vs fp16 baseline.
4) Access: need ephemeral API keys + a small IP allowlist for our test runners. We will provide a minimal Lab guide (Drive link below) and a signed MSA addendum for SOC2 scoping.

Attachments: novus_mvp_prompt_set.csv (attached) and a short plan doc.

Next steps: If you confirm procurement OKs the SOC2 addendum and can spin up an ephemeral hyperscaler test endpoint by Thursday, we can kick the runs Friday morning PT and share a preliminary deck by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference

- Lab access: Drive folder shared (link below) with the runner repo, test scripts, and the prompt set. We created an ephemeral Redwood API key scoped to "bench-runner" that will be valid for 72 hours once you confirm the IP allowlist. Please reply with the allowlist or an Accept link.

Planned measurement outputs (what you'll see in the deck):
- p50/p95/p99 server-side latency per config
- tokens/sec aggregate and per-GPU
- error/retry rate and 95% confidence intervals across runs
- delta table highlighting where Redwood's batching + KV-cache reduces p95 vs the hyperscaler baseline (if observed)
